title: Disentangling the origins of confidence in speeded perceptual judgments through multimodal imaging
description: Simultaneous EEG and fMRI recordings from healthy volunteers who reported their confidence in the accuracy of decisions they either committed themselves or merely observed. The dataset supports analysis of postdecisional contributions to metacognition and includes raw fMRI, BrainVision EEG, T1 anatomical scans and field maps, along with preprocessed EEG and fMRI derivatives.
methods_description: EEG was recorded concurrently with fMRI. MR-gradient artifacts were removed by sliding window template subtraction, and ballistocardiogram artifacts were removed in BrainVision Analyzer 2. Data were band-pass filtered at 1-10 Hz, epoched around response onset, re-referenced to a common average, and cleaned with ICA and dipole localization in EEGLAB. fMRI was modeled with a GLM using regressors for the active and observation conditions, parametrically modulated by confidence, response time, and perceptual evidence. Group-level results used cluster-extent FWE correction.
